name: sse4_crc32
workload: CRC-32 checksum of a single 1KB buffer and of random buffers up to 4KB, single-threaded, Node.js native addon
claimed_speedup: ~27x faster on a 1KB buffer (26ms vs 699ms) and up to 31.74x faster on buffers up to 4KB (62ms vs 1968ms)
hardware: MacBook Air, Intel Core i7, 8GB RAM
tradeoffs: Requires SSE4.2 hardware support (falls back to software CRC32 otherwise); this is CRC32C (Castagnoli polynomial) via the hardware CRC32 instruction, not the CRC-32/ISO-HDLC polynomial used by zlib's crc32(), so it is not a drop-in replacement for zlib's checksum without a polynomial change.
caveats: Blog benchmark compares the native SSE4.2 addon against a pure-JavaScript table-based/direct CRC32 implementation, not against a native C baseline like zlib's crc32(); compiler flags are not stated; the post is from 2013 and no updated benchmarks exist. Voxer/sse4_crc32 on GitHub is a stale fork; the canonical, actively-starred repo is anandsuresh/sse4_crc32 (same author's original), used here.
found_via: Blogs / talks: HN Algolia search "crc32c hardware accelerated" -> Voxer Engineering Blog, "Hardware-accelerated CRC-32 library for Node.js" (2013-12-02)
